ideas.title: See by clapping
ideas.critique: Seeing sound is new for the island: the traced arrival-time hits on real geometry and the convolved impulse response give it a sense it never had, and the hide-and-seek goal gives that sense a use. The risk is that the splats look like generic sparkles and the wave is hard to read. If the ring of arrivals and the lit faces of the trees don't read clearly, it is just glitter in the dark.

ideas.title: Burning glass
ideas.critique: A traced caustic that really drives a heat and ignition grid joins light and physics in a way only a path tracer can, and it puts fire on the island for the first time. Fire spreading over grass is a familiar game effect, though, and as play it is mostly aim-and-wait. It holds up only if the spot truly has to be sharp to burn.

ideas.title: Skipping stones
ideas.critique: The skimming model and ripple rings on a height field are real physics, and there is a clear score to beat, so players come back. It is also the most expected beach mini game on the list. What makes it worth doing is whether the rings stay on the water and the spin and angle really matter.

ideas.title: Stones that ring
ideas.critique: Modal synthesis from the FEM of each real mesh means every object sounds like its own shape, which the island has never had and few games do. It is engineering you can build more on. The lithophone goal is thin unless the search by ear is fun, and a film can easily turn into tapping with no visible payoff.

ideas.title: Pump the swing
ideas.critique: Parametric pumping is a nice true mechanism with a rhythm and a launch for distance. Still, a swing is a stock playground prop, and the slackening rope and ragdoll jump are where it will most likely look toy-like. It is a solid but predictable addition.

ideas.title: Paper planes
ideas.critique: This is the third white sheet in the air in a row. Fold-dependent trim is a real step for the sheet project, but a watcher sees one more paper drifting over the meadow. It only escapes repetition if the fold really decides the flight, so that different folds visibly glide, loop or dive.

ideas.title: The sand castle and the tide
ideas.critique: A wetness-dependent angle of repose is a real mechanism the sand rule lacked, and building against the tide is play people return to. But the island has already had sand piling and slumping in dunes, and a tide eating the work is close to its flooding and burying events.

ideas.title: Walk into the camera obscura
ideas.critique: The image is optically real, but the payoff is the same as the last post: the island upside down through a lens. Live and sharper is a modest step, and once the trick is seen there is nothing to do with it.

ideas.title: Tug of war
ideas.critique: Creatures on a rope pulling against each other was already done with Tied together. Foot friction per ground material is a small addition, and as pitched the player only watches. This is an expected creature-interaction scene.

ideas.title: Skating on the glass sea
ideas.critique: Grooves that stay and scatter light in the tracer are a real step on the frozen sea and a decent showcase for materials. Even so, people sliding over the glass sea is what the last ice post showed, and drawing with blades is a pleasant toy rather than a goal.
